committee: CC Affordable Housing Trust Fund Board
overview: The CC Affordable Housing Trust Fund Board oversees municipal affordable housing planning, funding allocations, and project support in Medford. Meeting in the archive across 11 sessions from November 2024 to September 2026, the board established foundational governance documents, coordinated funding programs, and worked on regulatory housing initiatives. During this time, the board drafted and approved a five-year affordable housing action plan and secured appropriations from the Community Preservation Act. At its most recent meeting, the board reviewed standardized developer application templates, examined calculation formulas for fractional payments and zoning incentives, and received updates on an upcoming housing resource fair.

threads.name: Five-Year Affordable Housing Action Plan
threads.summary: The board initiated work on its action plan through a subcommittee tasked with collecting demographic data and conducting stakeholder focus groups (M01#3, M02#3, M02#4). Following provider focus groups, the board organized public workshops and community sessions to gather input on housing costs and local priorities (M03#2, M04#3, M05#1). The board presented the draft five-year plan and local housing data at a public meeting in July 2025 (M07#5). In October 2025, the board voted to approve the final five-year action plan for submission to the City Council (M10#5).

threads.name: Declaration of Trust execution
threads.summary: The board reviewed legal counsel's revisions to the Declaration of Trust regarding signature authority and trustee removal procedures (M01#4). Signing was briefly postponed to allow for in-person notarization of the document (M02#2). In January 2025, board members signed the finalized Declaration of Trust before a notary for recording at the Registry of Deeds (M03#1).

threads.name: Developer funding applications and guidelines
threads.summary: Following an initial developer inquiry, the board began drafting formal application guidelines and loan documents based on municipal models (M04#5). The board approved an amended developer application and a draft Notice of Funding Availability pending legal review (M05#2, M06#2). After discussing whether to shift to a rolling application model, the board determined that the Declaration of Trust already authorized rolling submissions (M08#2, M10#7). The board returned to application guidelines in September 2026, reviewing draft standardized templates and long-term operating budget requirements for developers (M11#7).

threads.name: Community Preservation Act funding and Trust revenue
threads.summary: The board sought an initial $250,000 allocation from the Community Preservation Committee, which was subsequently approved by the City Council (M01#5, M04#4). Trustees later approved requesting an additional $50,000 and held a joint meeting with the committee to coordinate housing development funding requests (M06#4, M09#1). An application for $550,000 in fiscal year 2026 funds was submitted and accepted for presentation (M10#4). In September 2026, the board received status updates on an upcoming funding application for fiscal year 2027 (M11#9).

threads.name: Zoning coordination, linkage fees, and fractional payments
threads.summary: The board monitored comprehensive city zoning overhauls, including corridor incentives, MBTA Communities compliance, and cash-in-lieu options (M02#5, M03#4). The board voted to support the sale of city parcels on McCormick Avenue to fund a nexus study for affordable housing linkage fees (M05#3). Councilor Matt Leming later presented a resolution proposing fractional payments to the trust under inclusionary zoning provisions (M10#3). By September 2026, the linkage nexus study was finalized, and trustees examined calculation spreadsheets for fractional cash-in-lieu payments and revised formulas for zoning incentive bonuses (M11#4, M11#5, M11#6).

threads.name: Affordable housing development proposals and loans
threads.summary: The board monitored the pipeline of city-owned land requests for proposals and non-profit development inquiries (M02#6, M04#5). Metro Community Housing presented a request for up to $200,000 to resolve utility and cost overruns on a 3-unit development at 703 Fellsway West, prompting the board to ask for cost breakdowns (M08#1). The board subsequently reviewed draft loan and mortgage agreements for a $100,000 loan to Medford Community Housing for the 703 Fellsway West project (M10#6). In September 2026, staff reported that the Medford Housing Authority was expected to submit a funding request for Phase 2 of the Walkman Court project (M11#3).
